Markets can be created for different types of customers depending on how you sell. Each market type uses a different kind of condition to define its audience.
Country or region markets are displayed to customers based on their geographic location. These markets are used for cross-border and international selling.

When a customer visits your online store, their location is determined and they're matched to the appropriate country or region market. The customer then receives the experience that you've configured for that market, including currency, language, product availability, and theme customizations. A
country or region market can contain a single country or multiple countries.
Single-country markets contain one country or region. When you create a single-country market, the currency is automatically set to that country's local currency.

Multi-country markets contain more than one country or region. When you create a multi-country market, the currency customization is set to use local currencies by default. Local currencies are activated so that each country displays prices in its own currency.
A sub-region market targets a specific state or province, instead of a whole country. Use one when you want different shipping for part of a country.
On a sub-region market, you can customize only the shipping options. Everything else, such as currency, catalogs, theme, and domain, is inherited from the parent market.

Retail markets use POS locations as their condition. A retail market can target all POS locations, or specific POS locations. Retail customers are also part of a regional market based on the POS location's address, which means that a retail transaction can be associated with both a retail market and
a country or region market.

You can include company locations in B2B markets in three different ways: * All company locations in all regions: Includes all company locations, regardless of where they're located. * All company locations within a region: Includes all company locations shipping to addresses in the selected

regions. As you add more company locations that meet this criteria, they're automatically matched to these markets. * Specific company locations: Includes only the company locations you specify, regardless of where they're shipping to.

Channel markets use sales channels as their condition. A channel market can contain a single sales channel, or a group of channels sharing the same customizations. Channel markets let you set product availability, pricing, and currency for the specific sales channels that you sell through, such as
Google & YouTube, Facebook & Instagram, or TikTok.

When you create a channel market, the connected sales channels inherit the parent country or region market's catalog and currency by default. You can customize the channel market to set separate product availability, pricing, or currency that meets the channel's own requirements.

You can use all market types in the same store. Markets of different types can overlap, in which case the customer's experience is based on which settings are the most specific: * B2B markets are more specific than retail markets. Retail markets are more specific than country or region markets. *

When a customer qualifies for markets of multiple types, the more specific market type takes priority for how your market customizations take effect. * Catalogs from all applicable markets are combined, so customers can access products from all relevant catalogs.
When inheriting customizations: * Customizations from the same market type parent are combined. * Customizations from a different market type parent are overridden by the more specific type.
Country or region markets are available on all Shopify plans. There's no limit to the number of country or region markets you can create.
Sub-region markets are available as an early access feature. Features and functionality might change before general availability.
Retail markets are available for all Shopify plans. Customizing catalogs to use with retail markets requires Shopify POS Pro or the Plus plan.

On the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans, you can assign up to 3 active catalogs across all your B2B markets. Assigning 3 catalogs to one B2B market uses the full limit. You need to remove or draft an existing assignment before you can add catalogs to another market. On the Shopify Plus plan, you can
create an unlimited number of B2B market catalogs.
You can create markets from the Markets page in your Shopify admin to define where and how you sell to different customer groups.

When you create a Shopify store, the following markets are created for you automatically: * Domestic market: Your store's home country or region, as determined by your store's address and currency. This is your domestic market and represents the default customer experience. The country in your
domestic market is set as your backup region by default. * International market: A curated list of countries or regions where merchants similar to you also sell. This market is inactive by default.

In the Includes section, click Add condition. This condition defines which of your customers the market is displayed to: * To create a Regional market, select Regions, and then select the country or regions to create a market for. * To create a sub-region market, select Regions, open the country you

want to target, and then select the states or provinces to create a market for. Learn more about sub-region markets. * To create a B2B market, select Company locations, and then select the company locations to create a market for. To limit the market to one area, use the in filter to display only

company locations in a specific region or sub-region, such as a state or province. * To create a Retail market, select POS locations, and then select the retail locations to create a market for. * To create a Channel market, select Channels, and then select the sales channels to create a market for.
In the Inherited section, review the customizations for your new market. These settings are inherited from your store defaults, or from a parent market if the new market has one.
After you make a change, the setting is moved from the Inherited section to the Customized section.

If you create a market as a draft, or if you don't already ship to all the countries in a new market, then the market is inactive by default. Customers in inactive markets can't complete a purchase, and receive the backup region experience when they visit your store.

Markets for a customer are automatically determined by using the following information: * When a customer first visits your store, their geographic location is determined by using their IP address, and they're matched to the appropriate market. * The customer's browser language preferences are used

to determine which language to display, if you've configured multiple languages for that market. * If a customer arrives on a market-specific domain, subdomain, or subfolder (for example, yourstore.com/fr/), then they get the experience for that market. * If a customer manually chooses a different
country or language by using your store's selectors, then their preference is saved and used for future visits.

Different countries and regions have different expectations for how prices are displayed. For example, customers in Europe expect tax-inclusive prices, but customers in the United States expect tax to be added during checkout. Showing the wrong format creates confusion.
You can choose whether you want to automatically or manually localize your customers. By default, automatic redirection is activated in new stores, and automatic language detection is deactivated.

A customer's shipping address determines the final experience they receive. For example, if a customer from the United States is shopping online in USD but enters a Canadian shipping address at checkout, then their experience is updated to match the Canada market, including currency and any other

Markets form a hierarchy based on their conditions: * A market with broader conditions is a parent market of a market with more specific conditions. * A market with more specific conditions is a submarket of the broader market.
If a new market is determined to be within an existing market, then it's considered a submarket.

Submarkets inherit the currency of their parent market by default. * Customizing the currency on a submarket overrides the parent's currency. If a submarket has multiple parent markets with different currencies, then the currency that best matches the customer's local currency is used. If no
currencies match, then the most recently updated customization is prioritized.

If the same product exists in both a parent market and submarket catalog at different prices, then the submarket's price is used. If the same product exists in multiple parent catalogs at different prices, then the lowest price is displayed.

A business entity is the legal entity that processes payments for orders in a market. If your business has different legal entities in different countries or regions, then you can assign specific business entities to specific markets so that payments are processed through the correct entity.

By default, all orders in your store are processed through your primary Shopify Payments account, which is associated with your store's home country. If you have multiple Shopify Payments accounts for different legal entities in different countries, then you can assign each entity to the appropriate
market.
This is important for businesses that need to comply with local payment regulations, simplify tax reporting, or manage payouts in different currencies through local bank accounts.

When you use multiple business entities, payouts for each entity are deposited into the bank account associated with that entity's Shopify Payments account. Each entity can have its own payout currency and schedule.
Business entities are available on the Plus plan only.

Business entities are relevant only for stores using Shopify Payments with multiple accounts. * Changing the business entity for a market affects only new orders. Existing orders continue to be associated with the business entity that was active when the order was placed. * If you don't add a

business entity customization to a market, then orders in that market are processed through your default Shopify Payments account. * Some regions have regulations about which entity can process payments for customers in that region. Verify with a legal or finance expert that your business entity
assignments comply with local requirements.

A domain and language customization is a combination of a URL structure and a language for a specific market. When a customer visits your store, their location is used to identify their market and direct them to the appropriate domain and language.

orders.

Each market can have a currency customization that determines what currency is displayed to customers in that market. When a customer visits your store, their market is identified and prices are displayed in the currency configured for that market.

locator: Add a currency customization to a market, step 5
quote: Select your exchange rate settings: * Select Dynamic to automatically convert prices. Prices are converted using the current market exchange rate, updated regularly.
